page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance configured with 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. The system features a shared CPU allocation model and provides 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU.

The primary hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be attached for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The qualitative cost profile of this instance is shaped by its shared CPU allocation, which offers a more economical entry point for GPU-heavy workloads compared to dedicated CPU configurations, though it introduces potential CPU resource contention. The high memory capacity and dual GPU configuration make this instance profile appropriate for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science tasks, and graphics rendering that require significant VRAM and system memory but do not demand sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance.
